Recommended verification: derive dependency sets from every convolution and gate path. For stride-one stacks, the maximum receptive-field width is R=1+Σ(k−1)d, counting every convolution; dilation can leave gaps. Use explicit left padding d(k−1), then perturb future tokens and positions outside the derived span: earlier outputs must remain unchanged. Gradient checks supplement perturbations but can miss dependencies through saturated gates. Mask embeddings and padded states after biased convolutions/residual updates; exclude padding from loss and read the final nonpadding position, never count−1. These checks follow [PyTorch convolution semantics](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.nn.Conv1d.html).

For baseline-equivalent initialization, copy shared baseline tensors explicitly; identical seeds alone do not preserve initialization after adding modules. Initialize gates to an exact neutral effect—e.g., 2·sigmoid(0)=1—and compare features/logits before training. Register gates before optimizer construction, or use [add_param_group](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.optim.Adam.html); assert every trainable parameter’s identity occurs exactly once, then verify expected gradients and parameter updates. Save architecture configuration and state_dict; instantiate the actual generated predictor, load strictly, call eval(), and compare features, candidate scores and rankings across padded/short histories and all category routes. [PyTorch serialization guidance](https://docs.pytorch.org/tutorials/beginner/saving_loading_models) supports this workflow.

Activation-patching interpretation requires architectural caution: if raw embeddings feed gates in every residual block, patching one hidden state leaves downstream embedding-to-gate paths active. Consequently, incomplete recovery cannot establish that the patched representation lacks information or that earlier layers are unnecessary. This is a graph-based inference: intervene on embedding inputs and gate paths jointly, or isolate specific paths; report intervention scope, corruption method and score metric. [Patching research](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.16042) shows conclusions depend substantially on these experimental choices.
